name: Yannick Traoré-Skalický
location: Pilsen Veil, working out of a rented rehearsal bay in a building called the Meridian Hive
description:
Yannick is medium height and all kinetic energy, the kind of person who cannot sit without some part of him moving — tapping, shifting, bouncing a knee. His father's Malian bone structure and his mother's Czech coloring have given him an angular face with warm undertones, a combination he's leaned into with bioluminescent freckles across his cheeks and nose that glow soft amber under low light. He keeps his hair short except for a single long braid at his nape he wraps in conductive thread that connects to a personal haptic rig — his main instrument. His hands are covered in small calluses from years of dance and from the contact rigs he builds himself from salvaged holo-projector parts.

He makes work that lives at the intersection of choreography and holographic installation: his pieces require live performers moving through interactive holo-environments that respond to their bodies, creating something that is neither dance nor sculpture nor light show but something without a clean category name. He has a Tier 3 sponsorship from Axiom's cultural subdivision that he accepted last year with considerable public hand-wringing and that he still hasn't entirely made peace with. He is the most anxious person in any room who appears to be the least anxious person in that room.

core_fears: That the Axiom sponsorship has already changed what he makes and he can't see it from inside
That Threshold Body will fall apart because he can't manage people as well as he can manage movement
core_desires: A work that is genuinely impossible to categorize — something that breaks the taxonomy entirely
For the four people in his company to be financially stable; this desire embarrasses him and he rarely says it
coping_mechanisms: Physical exhaustion through training — choreographs his own anxiety into rehearsal
Performing the persona of someone who has resolved the Axiom question in order to avoid having to actually resolve it
blind_spots: He uses the company's artistic vision as a reason not to consult them on decisions that affect their lives
He is genuinely unaware of how often he interrupts people
psychology.secret: The piece he's currently developing was partially inspired by a classified internal Axiom document he was accidentally cc'd on — a proposal to use his holo-environment technology as a template for crowd behavioral modeling in their commercial spaces. He has not reported this and is not sure what to do with the information.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast and conceptually dense, mixes choreographic terminology with tech-speak; occasionally Bambara phrases from his father's family, which surprises people
speech_patterns.cadence: Quick, runs ahead of itself, frequently interrupts his own sentences to redirect
verbal_tics: 'No but—' to redirect without meaning to dismiss
Gestures with his hands constantly in patterns that seem almost choreographic
example_lines: 'No but the holo isn't set dressing — the holo is the other dancer. It has to have the same weight, the same resistance, or the whole thing is a lie.'
'Axiom says the piece can run thirty minutes. We need forty-five. I said yes to thirty. Don't tell the company yet.'

story_hooks: Someone within Axiom's cultural division is pressuring him to include specific 'audience engagement metrics' in the new piece — metrics that would require behavioral data collection from audience members without their consent
One of his Threshold Body performers has found an illegal neural-sync rig that would allow genuine direct choreographic communication between dancers — and wants to use it in the next production
narrative_function: Local color for Pilsen Veil's arts scene; quest giver when Axiom's cultural division starts asking questions about his work that seem less about art than about something else; source of information about the community of performers and their precarious finances
augmentations: Bioluminescent freckles (amber, face and neck); haptic rig interface thread in signature braid; basic sub-dermal muscle-monitoring sensors used for choreographic feedback
daily_life: Morning physical training, afternoon rehearsal with Threshold Body, evenings split between technical rig work and the fraught administrative labor of keeping four performers paid under an Axiom contract that doesn't pay enough.
affiliation: Axiom Cultural Division (sponsorship, non-exclusive); Pilsen Veil Arts Community; his own company of four performers called Threshold Body

decision_rules: Protect the company's artistic integrity publicly even when compromising privately
Never cancel a rehearsal — the work is the only thing that holds everything else together
escalation_ladder: Deflects and redirects with energy and charm
Admits the problem but frames it as manageable
Breaks — usually in private, to whoever is nearest, then reconstructs the public face within hours

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately warm and interesting, disarming energy; hard to get a straight answer about his actual life
interpersonal_modes.friends: Relies on them heavily and guiltily, apologizes constantly for needing things

stress_responses.low: Increases rehearsal hours, pushes the company harder
stress_responses.medium: Goes very quiet mid-conversation, loses the thread, apologizes
stress_responses.high: Calls everyone together and runs a rehearsal that lasts until someone physically stops him

contradictions: He makes work about authentic embodied presence while performing a version of himself that is carefully managed at all times
habits: Leaves choreographic notation offerings to an E.L.F. he calls the Threshold Spirit before every opening night — actual movement scores, folded into the projection array
Rewrites the set list for every show until three hours before doors, which the company hates
breaking_points: A performer quitting because they can't live on what the company pays
Axiom placing a content restriction on a work already in progress

timeline.event: 2171 — Born in Pilsen Veil to a Malian father and Czech mother, both factory-shift workers
2187 — First choreographic work with borrowed holo-projectors in a parking structure
2193 — Founds Threshold Body with three collaborators
2199 — Accepts Axiom Cultural Division sponsorship after six months of refusing
2200 — Accidentally receives the classified Axiom behavioral modeling document
